channel.title: Finality
channel.description: Finality reports crypto news: protocol upgrades, network incidents, exchange and stablecoin developments, regulation and the projects shaping blockchain.

item.title: JPMorgan extends JPMD transfers to Ethereum
item.description: J.P. Morgan is extending JPMD to Ethereum, adding the network to the institutional transfer options already available on Base and widening its onchain reach.

item.title: Ledger reviews wallet sales after CryptoBilis-linked theft
item.description: Ledger is reviewing reseller controls after an implanted hardware component in wallets sold through CryptoBilis was linked to about $90 million in crypto theft.

item.title: Estimate Bridge Fee Tiers From Net Proceeds
item.description: Compare bridge quotes by what arrives after fees, then check route limits, token decimals and separate transaction costs before sending funds across chains.

item.title: How to Move Treasury Tokens for a Chain Incentive
item.description: Moving treasury tokens for a chain incentive means matching the approved allocation to the destination contract, transfer path and final on-chain state.

item.title: Vault Liquidity and Order Books Price Trades Differently
item.description: Pool swaps price against shared inventory, while order books match bids and asks; the better route depends on depth, execution control, fees and timing.

item.title: Which Fees Remain After You Cancel a Bridge Route?
item.description: Canceling a bridge route does not undo transactions already included on-chain: you may still pay for approval, source-chain gas and any completed bridge work.

item.title: A Stablecoin Funding Cutoff Is a Payment Deadline, Not a Network Rule
item.description: A funding cutoff is a provider’s processing deadline, not a stablecoin network shutdown; learn which rail, time zone and confirmation rule controls availability.

item.title: Swap Into the Fee Token a Cross-Chain Message Requires
item.description: A cross-chain message fee is paid in the token required by its source contract path; swap before sending, retain gas, and verify the live quote and accepted fee asset.

item.title: Cross-Chain Swap Stuck? Check Its State Before Retrying
item.description: A pending swap is a state problem, not a signal to submit again: verify the source transaction, route status and destination claim or refund path first.

item.title: When Cross-Chain Swap Auctions Make Sense
item.description: An auction can speed a cross-chain swap by paying from destination-chain liquidity first; the trade-off is solver capacity, route fees and delayed source settlement.

item.title: Bridge Funds to the NFT’s Chain Before You Buy
item.description: Bridge the payment asset and gas to the destination chain, verify the listing’s settlement network, then buy there; the NFT stays on its own chain.

item.title: EBA makes USDC the EU’s first significant e-money token
item.description: The EBA classified Circle’s USDC as the EU’s first significant e-money token, shifting oversight of its reserves, liquidity and redemption plans to EU level.

item.title: Why Token Approval and Swap Gas Estimates Change
item.description: Approval and swap estimates come from simulating specific calldata against current chain state; allowance, route, and execution path determine the gas limit.

item.title: Cross-chain swap rates are route prices, not token prices
item.description: Cross-chain swap rates depend on executable output after price impact, bridge fees, gas, settlement time, and failure risk; compare the full route, not its headline quote.

item.title: Check the destination before sending through a crypto bridge
item.description: A bridge transfer can settle on the wrong chain or into the wrong asset contract; verify the destination network, token representation, route and recipient first.

item.title: Circle plans entry into about 40 emerging markets
item.description: Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire says the issuer will pursue about 40 emerging markets as rising stablecoin demand pushes USDC toward mainstream use globally.

item.title: Exchange Maintenance Can Hold a Treasury Withdrawal Before Broadcast
item.description: Exchange maintenance can stop a treasury withdrawal before it reaches a blockchain. The transaction’s status shows whether the delay sits with the venue or network.

item.title: Should You Approve a Mantle Bridge Prompt Twice?
item.description: A repeated Mantle bridge approval signs an ERC-20 allowance change, not a second transfer; check the spender, amount and pending transaction before signing.

item.title: Hardware Wallets Can Sign Mantle Bridge Transactions
item.description: A hardware wallet can authorize Mantle bridge calls through an EVM wallet interface, but deposits, token approvals and Ethereum claims may each need separate signatures.

item.title: Recurring Treasury Transfers Need a Recovery Path
item.description: Recurring treasury transfers are safest when execution, recipient checks and token recovery sit in a narrowly scoped contract with explicit roles and limits.
